## Workflow conventions

- Branch per Linear issue: `feature/<sma-####>-<kebab-title>`. The branch name is pre-computed in each Linear ticket's `gitBranchName` field.
- Design artifacts per ticket (`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md`) land on the feature branch alongside the implementation — not pre-merged to `main`.
- **Keep the public mdBook (`docs/book/`) current — update it in the same PR as any user-facing change.** Before opening a PR, check whether the work changes public API, the quickstart/example flow, the crate roster (incl. a stub crate ascending to published), or a documented concept; if so, bring the affected `docs/book/src/*.md` page(s) into line on the same branch. The book is published from `main` and drifts silently otherwise — it sat as the untouched SMA-311 scaffold (13/17 pages still `> **Stub.**`) through all of Stage 1 before anyone noticed; SMA-423 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no book edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip. `mdbook build docs/book` must stay clean (`[output.linkcheck] warning-policy = "error"`).
- **Keep crate `README.md` files current — update the affected crate's README in the same PR as any change to its public surface.** Each of the ten published crates' `README.md` is its crates.io (and docs.rs landing-sidebar) page — no crate sets an explicit `readme`, so Cargo uses the default `README.md`. Before opening a PR, for every crate the work touches check whether the change affects that crate's public API / usage example, its install or feature story, or its published status (a stub ascending to published, a renamed/added feature flag); if so, bring its `crates/<crate>/README.md` into line on the same branch — and also the facade `crates/paigasus-helikon/README.md` and the root `README.md` whenever the crate roster or the feature → module map changes. README install snippets deliberately use drift-free `cargo add` (no hardcoded versions), so a routine version bump alone needs no README edit. Like the mdBook, the READMEs drift silently otherwise — they sat as untouched 3-line SMA-304 stubs (`Stub — see SMA-304`) through all of Stage 1 while ten crates shipped real implementations; SMA-424 is the one-time catch-up, and this rule keeps the backlog from rebuilding. A pure-internal change (refactor, CI, deps, release plumbing) needs no README edit — but make that a conscious call, not a silent skip.
- Commit prefix: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-### <message>` (e.g. `feat(facade): SMA-304 ...`).
- **PR titles must satisfy two independent rules from `pr-title.yml`** (`amannn/action-semantic-pull-request`):
  1. **Full Conventional Commits format.** The action enforces a valid `type(scope):` prefix from the action's configured `types` list — independent of the subject regex. `SMA-317 add anthropic provider` (no prefix) fails; `feat(providers-anthropic): SMA-317 add anthropic provider` passes.
  2. **Subject must start lowercase after the `SMA-###` prefix.** The `subjectPattern: ^([A-Z]{2,4}-\d+ )?[^A-Z].+$` rejects `feat(core): SMA-314 LlmAgent + ...` because `L` is uppercase; lead the subject with a lowercase verb (`add`, `wire`, `pin`, `promote`, `implement`, `fix`).
  Per-commit Conventional Commit titles on the feature branch don't trip either rule — only the PR title (which becomes the squashed `main` commit) is gated.
- Linear auto-closes the linked SMA-* issue when its PR merges; no manual status move needed.
- **Always implement GitHub Actions against the latest stable major**, pinned to a commit SHA (never a moving `@vN` tag), keeping the human-readable version as a trailing `# vX.Y.Z` comment **on the `uses:` line**, so the SHA is auditable. The comment must end with the version: Dependabot updates only a same-line comment that ends with the old version, so a version on its own line above the step goes stale on every bump (SMA-744). This rule applies only to pins of a tagged release. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is pinned to an untagged `master` commit, so it has no version comment. Do not add one, because no tag gives a correct version. The `gh-actions` Dependabot group sets no `update-types`, so its configuration permits major bumps in the same grouped PR. Do not depend on that: `actions/checkout` still sat on v6.0.2 until SMA-486 bumped it by hand, so **check for a new major by hand**. `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is a special case: it ships rolling branches and a periodically re-pointed `v1` tag, so confirm the direction (`ahead_by > 0, behind_by == 0`) before accepting any bump — the naive "bump to latest release" recipe once would have proposed an ~11-month downgrade. Independently and permanently: every site pinning it **must** pair the SHA with an explicit `with: toolchain: …`, because a SHA ref carries no toolchain selector. Recipes and history: `docs/runbooks/github-actions-pinning.md`.
- **After a PR merges to `main`, release-plz opens/updates a `chore: release` PR** (authored by the paigasusbot App) carrying the version bumps + CHANGELOG; in the normal flow **merging that PR is what publishes to crates.io** (the merged feature PR left versions matching the registry, so its own `main` push publishes nothing). The exception is a PR that bumps its own version — the stub-ascend ritual — which publishes on its own merge with no separate release PR. Check the release PR after every merge and watch its CI — its release-PR `cargo update` can pull a fresh advisory that reddens `audit`/`deny` on the bot PR **only** (independent of `main`); fix with a `chore(deps)` pin and release-plz regenerates the PR clean.

## CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs nine jobs on every PR (`commits` is PR-only; the other eight also run on push to `main`): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` (matrix `{ubuntu, macos, windows} × {stable, 1.94}`, `fail-fast: false`), `build-no-default-features`, `docs` (`RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`), `doc-coverage` (gated at `DOC_COVERAGE_THRESHOLD`, default 80%), `commits` (`convco check`), `sessions-it` (Postgres/Redis, path-filtered), and `markdown-lint`. The `paigasus-helikon-cli` crate is excluded from both the `missing_docs` lint and the coverage aggregator until its public API stabilizes.

`.github/workflows/integration.yml` runs `temporal-it` and `agentcore-image` as **signal-only** jobs, deliberately outside `ci.yml` so an expected flake cannot make "ci is red on `main`" meaningless. **Signal-only means *not listed as required*, never `continue-on-error`.**

`.github/workflows/msrv.yml` runs `cargo msrv --path crates/paigasus-helikon-core verify` as a non-required signal that the declared MSRV is truthful.

Supply-chain workflows (`audit.yml`, `deny.yml`, `sbom.yml`) are separate from `ci.yml` because they have independent triggers and failure semantics. `audit.yml` and `deny.yml` both run on push to `main`, PRs, a daily cron, and `workflow_dispatch`, so `main` is re-evaluated daily at exactly PR severity.

**To read an audit verdict, use the Checks API, not the legacy commit-status API** — the latter returns only `CodeRabbit` on this repo, rendering a confident `state: success` that contains no audit verdict whatsoever:

```bash
gh api repos/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/commits/main/check-runs \
  --jq '.check_runs[] | select(.name=="audit" or .name=="deny") | {name, status, conclusion}'
```

Note also that the `scheduled-audit` job's green status means nothing at any severity — read the *run* conclusion, never that job's status.

The required-status-check contexts gated on `main` are (bare job names, as posted by the GitHub Actions app): `fmt`, `clippy`, `test (ubuntu-latest, stable)`, `test (macos-latest, stable)`, `test (windows-latest, stable)`, `docs`, `doc-coverage`, `book-build`, `commits`, `pr-title`, `audit`, `deny`, `sessions-it`, `build-no-default-features`, `markdown-lint`. The macOS job is required because it is the only gate that compiles and runs the Seatbelt backend; the Windows job because it is the only gate that exercises the Windows timeout path in `paigasus-helikon-tools` — `cmd /C` process spawning and a `TerminateProcess`-based kill, which unlike the unix path has no process-group semantics and assigns a real exit code (SMA-569); `sessions-it` because it is the only gate that runs the live Postgres/Redis session backends; `build-no-default-features` because it is the only gate that compiles `runtime-axum` and `runtime-actix` with default features off. The canonical declaration is `.github/rulesets/main-protection-checks.json` (see CONTRIBUTING.md → "Repo configuration"). Other matrix variants (the `1.94` legs) run as signals only.

These pins are hand-bumped with nothing tracking them: `TEMPORAL_CLI_VERSION`/`TEMPORAL_CLI_SHA256` in `integration.yml`, `NIGHTLY_TOOLCHAIN` in `ci.yml`, `convco@…` in `ci.yml`'s `commits` job, `MDBOOK_VERSION`/`MDBOOK_LINKCHECK_VERSION` in `docs.yml`, and `markdownlint-cli2` via `package-lock.json`. **A checksum mismatch is never a signal to update the digest** — the causes are, in order, a truncated download, an upstream re-tag, and tampering; verify upstream independently first.

**The workspace needs no system `protoc`** (SMA-623): `temporalio-client`'s `vendored-protox` feature compiles the Temporal protos with `protox`. `ci.yml` sets `PROTOC` to a path that does not exist, and `build-no-default-features` asserts that the feature is active. If a build fails with "Could not find `protoc`", do not add a `protoc` install — find which build script calls it. Rationale and recovery: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "protoc and protox".

Job-by-job rationale, the audit/deny signal semantics, and the incident history behind all of the above: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md`.

**GitHub's 10 GB Actions cache limit is a standing constraint, not a one-time cleanup** (SMA-618): it is GitHub's **default**, not a hard ceiling — a repo admin, org owner or enterprise owner can raise it (user-owned repos up to 10 TB) at additional storage cost, and SMA-618 deliberately chose to fit inside it rather than pay. Enforced at 10 **GiB** (10,737,418,240 bytes) despite the "10 GB" wording. Going over fails nothing — it just triggers silent LRU eviction that makes CI legs run cold at random. `cache-budget.yml` monitors it daily and warns (never fails) above 8.5 GiB. Caches are saved **only** from `main` (`save-if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}` on every `Swatinem/rust-cache` site) so a PR job can still restore an entry `main` wrote but never writes a competing `refs/pull/N/merge` entry that evicts it. The `CARGO_*`/`RUST*`-prefixed workflow env that `rust-cache` hashes into its key must stay byte-identical across every cache-bearing workflow, enforced by `scripts/check-cargo-profile-env-sync.sh` running as a step in `fmt`. `audit` and `deny` deliberately cache no `target/` directory — neither compiles the workspace, so it was pure waste against the fixed budget.  CI also sets **`CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: line-tables-only`** (SMA-618 PR 2), which measured a **16.5% cut in total cache bytes** — 14-29% on the `test` legs and exactly 0% on `clippy`/`docs`/`doc-coverage`, which are metadata-mode builds with no debug info to remove. (A local sample of the largest `.rlib` files suggested 79%; do not extrapolate an aggregate from its densest component.) Keeping line tables preserves file:line in panic backtraces. Like `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`, it is **inside** rust-cache's key, so it must be byte-identical in every cache-bearing workflow — adding it to one and not the rest silently splits the cache rather than failing. `prefix-key: v1` marks the post-PR-2 generation, so any surviving `v0-` entry is provably stale and safe to purge — note it **replaces** the default `v0-rust` entirely, so keys read `v1-<job>-...`, not `v1-rust-<job>-...`. `clippy` and `docs` share one entry via `shared-key: metadata`, with `clippy` the sole writer and `docs` carrying a literal `save-if: false`; exactly one site may save a shared key, and the guard enforces it. Full rationale: `docs/runbooks/ci-architecture.md` → "Actions cache budget".

The **`microvm`/forkd live-KVM path is not validated locally or in GitHub CI** — the dev host is arm64 macOS (no `/dev/kvm`) and GitHub runners have none. Validate it on a **GCP nested-virtualization VM** (Ubuntu 24.04 — the forkd binaries need glibc ≥ 2.38; Intel `n2`) per `docs/runbooks/forkd-live-validation.md`. The `tests/forkd_live.rs` tests are env-gated (`FORKD_URL` / `FORKD_TOKEN` / `FORKD_SNAPSHOT`) and loud-skip when no controller is configured, so `cargo test` stays green without one.

## Local hooks

Hooks are managed via `cargo-husky` (user-hooks mode) and live in `.cargo-husky/hooks/`. They install into `.git/hooks/` on the next dev-dep realization of `paigasus-helikon`. To force a re-install after editing one: `rm -rf target/debug/build/cargo-husky-* && cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`.

- **`commit-msg`** — runs `convco check --from-stdin` (enforces the `.versionrc` allowlist).
- **`pre-commit`** — intentional no-op (`exit 0`). The file exists to claim the slot so future cargo-husky upgrades don't fill it in with surprise behavior.
- **`pre-push`** — runs `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `convco check <merge-base>..HEAD`. Catches the three fastest CI gates pre-push; deliberately omits `cargo test` and `cargo doc` (too slow for every push). Bypass for WIP branches: `git push --no-verify`.

Three rules here are easy to get wrong, and each has already cost a debugging session:

- **The re-install silently does nothing inside a git worktree** — cargo-husky searches for a `.git` *directory* and a worktree's is a file, so it installs nothing and the old hook keeps running. Run the re-install from the **main checkout**, and verify with `grep` against the installed copy rather than assuming.
- **Never hand-copy a hook onto `.git/hooks/<name>`** — on this machine the Entire CLI owns `pre-push` and chains to `.git/hooks/pre-push.pre-entire`, which is where the cargo-husky hook actually lives. Check for a `.pre-entire` sibling first and install into that slot.
- **The convco baseline must be a merge-base, not a branch tip** — `convco check A..B` silently falls back to walking the entire history when `A` is not an ancestor of `B`, rejecting correct branches with failures the author did not write.

Mechanics and the SMA-547 postmortem: `docs/runbooks/local-hooks.md`.

1686	/// way across every subject, rather than re-deriving Anthropic's in-band error
1687	/// shape a second time in a different harness. Functionally the two
1688	/// mechanisms are indistinguishable to this driver either way: `model.rs`'s
1689	/// `Some(Err(e)) => { yield Err(...); return; }` arm returns as soon as it
1690	/// observes *any* transport-level error, before it would ever get to parse a
1691	/// subsequent `error` frame.
1692	///
1693	/// # Three things specific to this provider
1694	///
1695	/// **`message_delta` carries the stop reason AND usage in the same event**
1696	/// (see [`message_delta`]'s doc). That is what gives `CancelAfterStopReason` an
1697	/// observable edge to gate on at all — unlike `openai_chat`/`litellm`, whose
1698	/// finish-reason chunk is silent and needs a synthetic *following* usage chunk
1699	/// for the gate to sit after.
1700	///
1701	/// **`message_start` also emits a `Usage`** (`stream.rs`'s `MessageStart` arm),
1702	/// which makes the harness's own "at least one `Usage` observed" floor for
1703	/// `CancelAfterStopReason` vacuous for this subject — it is satisfied by
1704	/// `message_start` alone, whether or not the gate sits in the right place. The
1705	/// harness's `floor_violation` doc records this narrowing explicitly. The only
1706	/// guard left for this scenario on this subject is the provenance comment on
1707	/// its `script` match arm below, which states in prose where `gate_after`
1708	/// counts to and why — treat that comment as load-bearing, not decoration.
1709	///
1710	/// **`message_start` contains a literal `"stop_reason":null`.** A naive scan
1711	/// for the substring `stop_reason` would therefore match the very first event
1712	/// of every script, whether or not a stop reason was ever encoded.
1713	/// [`STOP_REASON_MARKER`] scans for the populated-string shape instead, pinned
1714	/// against `message_start`'s `null` by `scan_finds_only_a_populated_stop_reason`
1715	/// — the only detector for `ErrorAfterStopReason` degrading into
1716	/// `ErrorMidGeneration`: `classify` and `floor_violation` don't distinguish
1717	/// the two by `Usage` count, only by `Finish`/`Err` presence and ordering,
1718	/// which already match for both (see `scan_finds_only_a_populated_stop_reason`'s
1719	/// own doc for the full argument).

1721	/// # `ToolCallCleanStop` never splits `input_json_delta`

1728	/// name" — no committed capture grounds Anthropic ever doing that, and
1729	/// inventing the split would fabricate a shape per this file's provenance

1731	/// "exactly one, not zero" on this shape: the translator's `name_emitted` flag

1982	                content_block_start_text(),

1992	        let through_stop = || {

1994	            chunks.push(content_block_stop());
1995	            chunks.push(message_delta("end_turn", 5));
1996	            chunks

1999	        let (chunks, gate_after, ending) = match scenario {

2003	            // and `usage.output_tokens` are pulled from the fixture
2004	            // (`message_delta("end_turn", 5)`); `message_start`'s `id`/
2005	            // `model` and the delta text are this module's own values, not
2006	            // the fixture's `"msg_01"`/`"claude-sonnet-4-6"`/`"Hello"`/
2007	            // `" world"`.

2012	            }

2014	            // body simply ends — no `message_stop` — so the translator's
2015	            // buffered stop reason has to be flushed by the EOF path
2016	            // (`MessageTranslator::finish`, called from `model.rs`'s
2017	            // `None =>` arm). Matches `eof_after_message_delta.txt`'s event
2018	            // sequence and `stop_reason`/`usage` values exactly; `id`/`model`

2021	            Scenario::TruncatedAfterStopReason => (through_stop(), None, Ending::Clean),

2024	            // in `eof_mid_content_block.txt` (see the module doc's provenance

# SMA-567 stream conformance extensions — implementation plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Close the SMA-533 coverage gaps that captured traffic supports, and pin the rest in a new
`UNCAPTURED` table.

**Architecture:** Extend `tests/provider-stream-conformance` in its own style: new `Scenario`
variants, new `classify` rules (proven by `Fake`s), new `floor_violation` checks (proven by direct
`floor_violation` tests), and an `Outcome::Uncaptured` outcome cross-checked against a pinned table.
One doc sentence goes into `core`, and one test goes into `providers-bedrock`.

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.94, tokio, `serde_json`, `aws-smithy-eventstream` (already a dependency).

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-sma-567-stream-conformance-extensions-design.md`. Read
it before every task. Section numbers below (§) refer to it.

## Global Constraints

- Worktree: `/Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567`, branch
  `feature/sma-567-extend-the-stream-conformance-suite-to`. Use absolute paths. Never run
  `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git reset`, `git stash` or any command that moves `HEAD`.
- Work in the foreground. Do not background a `cargo` run. Do not end a task before its command
  reports a final status.
- Suite test command: `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance`.
- Before each commit: `cargo fmt --all` and
  `cargo clippy -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Commit messages: `<type>(<scope>): SMA-567 <lowercase subject>`. Scopes must match `.versionrc`.
  There is no `tests` scope. Use `test(providers)` for suite and provider-test commits, and
  `docs(core)` and `docs(docs)` for §6.6. End each message with
  `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- Stage explicit paths only. Never `git add -A` or `git add .` (`.env` is not ignored).
- Provenance rule (§1, §6.9): every new fixture is transcribed from a named captured file, and each
  edit is listed in its comment. Never invent an event.
- Decline and uncaptured reasons in `tests/conformance.rs` are **literal strings** copied by hand.
  Never look them up from the tables (header rule 1 of `tests/conformance.rs`).
- **Stop rule (§7):** when the full suite fails on a real subject after you add a rule, do not change
  the rule, a fixture or a translator to make it pass. Stop and report the subject, the scenario and
  the `observed:` line.
- Every exhaustive `match` on `Scenario` stays exhaustive, with no `_` arm (see
  `bedrock::fixture_finish_reason`).

## Review Focus

1. **`Err` then `Usage` then something else.** Option B exempts only `Usage`. `Err, Usage,
   TokenDelta` must still give `EventAfterError`. Test in Task 2.
2. **Gemini's `"finishReason": "STOP"` with a space.** A byte-faithful transcription makes
   `encodes_stop_reason` return `false`, and the scenario fails with `StopReasonDeclarationMismatch`.
   Test in Task 6.
3. **A blank-id group with two names under assertion 10.** It must be skipped, not parsed as one
   concatenated value. Test in Task 3.
4. **A subject that reports `Uncaptured` for a pair that `DECLINED` lists, or the reverse.** It must
   fail. Test in Task 1.
5. **Empty deltas in the channel order.** Anthropic's `content_block_start` for text carries
   `"text":""`. If the translator emits an empty `TokenDelta` there, it is a run. The declared order
   comes from the capture, and the stop rule applies if they disagree. Recorded in Task 5.

---

### Task 0: File the three follow-up Linear issues (coordinator, not a subagent)

- [x] **Step 1:** In the Linear project `Paigasus Helikon` (team `Sven Maschek`), check with
  `list_issues` that no matching issue exists. Then create three issues, related to SMA-567, with
  the labels `area:providers`, `area:testing` and `Improvement`:
  1. Capture a reasoning stream for `bedrock`, `litellm` and `openai/responses`. The SMA-585
     gpt-5-mini captures are the first input.
  2. Capture a parallel tool-call stream for `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `litellm`, `openai/chat` and
     `openai/responses`, if possible with interleaved arguments. Record spec §3.5.
  3. Capture a zero-argument tool-call stream for `anthropic`, `bedrock`, `gemini`, `litellm` and
     `openai/chat`, including a stream with no argument deltas. Note Gemini's `"null"` arguments.

  Each issue's acceptance criteria says that it closes only when its `UNCAPTURED` rows are removed,
  by a capture or by a reviewed move to `DECLINED`.
- [x] **Step 2:** Recorded: reasoning `SMA-858`, parallel `SMA-859`, zero-arg `SMA-860`. The tasks below cite them.

### Task 1: `Outcome::Uncaptured` and the `UNCAPTURED` table

**Files:**
- Modify: `tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/lib.rs` (`Outcome`, `assert_conforms`,
  `assert_declines_match`, tests module)
- Modify: `tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/declines.rs`
- Modify: `tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs` (header rule 1 doc only)

**Interfaces:**
- Produces: `Outcome::Uncaptured(&'static str)`;
  `pub const UNCAPTURED: &[(&str, Scenario, &str, &str)]` (subject, scenario, reason, follow-up id),
  empty in this task; `#[cfg(test)] const UNCAPTURED_SCENARIOS: &[Scenario]` (the allow-list),
  empty in this task. Later tasks add rows to both.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing tests.** In the `lib.rs` tests module, give the mock `Subject` a
  field `uncaptured: &'static [(Scenario, &'static str)]` (default `&[]`) that `stream()` returns
  as `Outcome::Uncaptured`. Add three `#[should_panic]` tests that mirror the three decline tests:
  - `an_unpinned_uncaptured_pair_fails` — expected `"unexpected uncaptured"`;
  - `a_pinned_uncaptured_pair_that_stopped_happening_fails` — expected `"is pinned as uncaptured"`.
    Drive it with a test-only table, see Step 3;
  - `a_drifted_uncaptured_reason_fails` — expected `"drifted"`.

  Add `an_uncaptured_outcome_for_a_declined_pair_fails` — the subject reports `Uncaptured` with the
  `DECLINED` reason for `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop`. It must panic with `"unexpected uncaptured"`.
  In `declines.rs` tests, add:
  - `no_pair_is_in_both_tables`;
  - `every_uncaptured_subject_is_registered`;
  - `every_follow_up_is_a_linear_id` (each fourth field matches `^SMA-\d+$`, checked without a
    regex crate);
  - `every_scenario_has_a_serving_subject` (for each `Scenario::ALL` entry, some name in
    `REGISTERED_SUBJECTS` is in neither table);
  - `uncaptured_rows_name_only_allow_listed_scenarios`.
- [ ] **Step 2:** Run the suite test command. Expected: compile failure on `Outcome::Uncaptured`.
- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** Generalise `assert_declines_match` into
  `fn assert_pinned_match(subject: &str, kind: PinnedKind, observed: &[(Scenario, &'static str)], pinned: &[(Scenario, &'static str)])`,
table, so that the table cites real identifiers.

### 6.8 Proving that each new rule can fail

This is the acceptance criterion "each new assertion has a non-conformant fake".

`conforming()` changes:

- `ReasoningCleanStop`: a `ReasoningDelta`, then the text, then one tool call, then `Usage` and
  `Finish(ToolCalls)`.
- `ParallelToolCallCleanStop`: two calls with two different `call_id`s. `fakes::tool` takes a
  `call_id` parameter.
- `ZeroArgToolCallCleanStop`: one call with one `{}` delta.

New `Fake` variants for the `classify` rules, each in `every_fake_is_rejected_with_its_classification`:

- `Fake::TokenAfterError`: append a `TokenDelta` to an error scenario. Rejected as
  `EventAfterError`.
- `Fake::ArgsNotJson`: replace the tool deltas with a truncated `{"city":`. Rejected as
  `ToolArgsNotJson`.
- `Fake::ProviderDataUnknownCall`: a call-scoped `ProviderData` for an id that no call used.
  Rejected as `ProviderDataUnknownCall`. Assertion 8 has no fake today.

A positive test: a call with blank arguments (no `args_delta` text) passes assertion 10.

The fakes never reach the floors (`fakes.rs` module doc). For each new floor, add a test that
calls `floor_violation` directly with `conforming(scenario)` changed in one place, and asserts the
exact violation:

- a reasoning run moved after the text run: `ChannelOrderMismatch`;
- no `ReasoningDelta`: `InsufficientEvidence`;
- a `None` channel order for `ReasoningCleanStop`: `InsufficientEvidence`;
- the arguments of the two calls swapped: `ToolCallsMismatch`;
- one `call_id` only in the parallel scenario: `InsufficientEvidence`;
- the zero-argument call with real arguments: `ToolCallsMismatch`;
- an `Err` in `CleanStop`: the no-`Err` floor;
- no `Usage` in `CleanStop`: `InsufficientEvidence`.

`the_conforming_fake_clears_every_floor` covers the three new scenarios.

For the `UNCAPTURED` cross-check, add the same three negative tests that the `DECLINED`
cross-check has: an unpinned pair, a stale row and a changed reason.

# Task 5 report: `ReasoningCleanStop` and the channel-order floor

Status: DONE_WITH_CONCERNS (one decision about the tool name, see "Concerns").

Commit: `526afd29 test(providers): SMA-567 add a reasoning channel-order scenario`

## What I implemented

### Harness (`src/lib.rs`)

- `Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop`, added to `ALL`, to `expects_stop_reason`, and to
  `scenario_all_is_exhaustive`.
- `pub enum Channel { Reasoning, Text, Tool }` (derives `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq`), with doc
  comments.
- The trait method `fn fixture_channel_order(&self, scenario: Scenario) -> Option<&'static [Channel]>`.
  It has no default.
- `Violation::ChannelOrderMismatch { expected: Vec<Channel>, observed: Vec<Channel> }`. Its doc says that it
  checks fidelity to the wire, not the contract.
- `floor_violation` has a new parameter `channel_order: Option<&[Channel]>`. `assert_conforms_with` passes
  `subject.fixture_channel_order(scenario)`. `ReasoningCleanStop` gets these floors:
  - the tool floors (a `ToolCallDelta` exists, and one carries the declared name);
  - the clean-stop `Finish` floor (a `Finish` exists and has the declared reason);
  - at least one `ReasoningDelta` (`"no ReasoningDelta: ..."`);
  - a declared order (`"the subject declares no channel order ..."`).
  For every scenario that declares `Some(order)`, the observed runs must equal the order. The new helper
  `channel_runs` maps the three delta kinds to channels, ignores all other events, and merges adjacent
  equal channels. An empty delta counts as a run.
- The `floor_violation` doc explains the new floors, the wire-fidelity scope (`core/src/model.rs:56-57`),
  and the empty-delta rule. The `fixture_finish_reason` doc now says "Exactly five".
- The mock `Subject`: `Subject::conforming(name)` now takes its declines and uncaptured pairs from the
  pinned tables for its name (`openai/chat`, `anthropic`, `bedrock`; any other name panics). The reasons are
  hand-written literals. It declares `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]` for `ReasoningCleanStop`. Two existing tests
  that override `declines` for `openai/chat` now include the reasoning decline.

### Fakes (`src/fakes.rs`)

- `conforming(ReasoningCleanStop)` is `ReasoningDelta`, `token("hi")`, the two tool deltas, `Usage`,
  `Finish(ToolCalls)`.
- `finish` and `declared_finish_reason` map `ReasoningCleanStop` to `ToolCalls`.
- New test-side `declared_channel_order(scenario)`: `Some(&[Reasoning, Text, Tool])` for
  `ReasoningCleanStop`, `None` otherwise. `the_conforming_fake_clears_every_floor` passes it.

### Tables (`src/declines.rs`)

- `DECLINED`: `gemini` / `ReasoningCleanStop` / "the request never enables thought parts, so none arrive on
  the wire"; `openai/chat` / `ReasoningCleanStop` / "the Chat Completions wire carries no reasoning text".
- `UNCAPTURED`: `bedrock`, `litellm`, `openai/responses` / `ReasoningCleanStop` / "no captured reasoning
  stream" / `SMA-858`.
- `UNCAPTURED_SCENARIOS = &[Scenario::ReasoningCleanStop]`.

### Subjects (`tests/conformance.rs`)

- `bedrock`, `litellm`, `openai/responses`: `Outcome::Uncaptured("no captured reasoning stream")`.
- `gemini`: `Outcome::Declined("the request never enables thought parts, so none arrive on the wire")`.
- `openai/chat`: `Outcome::Declined("the Chat Completions wire carries no reasoning text")`.
- These five subjects return `None` from `fixture_channel_order`, and their `script` and
  `fixture_finish_reason` matches stay exhaustive with no `_` arm.
- `anthropic` serves the scenario. `fixture_channel_order` is an exhaustive match. It returns
  `[Reasoning, Text, Tool]` for `ReasoningCleanStop` and `None` for every other scenario.
  `fixture_finish_reason` gives `ToolCalls`. `request()` offers the tool.
- The `anthropic` script is all of run C (`thinking_text_tool_use.txt`) in wire order:
  `message_start`, thinking block at index 0 (start, 15 `thinking_delta`s, `signature_delta` `SIG_FAKE_1`,
  stop), text block at index 1 (start, 12 `text_delta`s, stop), `tool_use` at index 2 (start, 4
  `input_json_delta`s including the empty first one, stop), `message_delta` (`tool_use`), `message_stop`.
  **No delta is merged.** The provenance comment on the script arm lists every edit:
  1. The `ping` event (lines 9-10) is dropped.
  2. The tool name `lookup_city_code` becomes `get_weather` (see "Concerns").
  3. `json!` writes the keys in sorted order and without the spaces of the source. The keys and values do
     not change.
  4. The comment line (line 1) of the source file is not sent.
- Reused helpers, because their shapes match the capture exactly: `thinking_start`, `thinking_delta`,
  `signature_delta`, `content_block_stop_at`, `input_json_delta_at`, `message_stop`.
- New helpers, because no existing helper matched the capture: `content_block_start_text_at`,
  `text_delta_at` (the old `content_block_start_text` and `text_delta` now call them with index 0),
  `tool_use_start_with_caller_at` (adds `"caller":{"type":"direct"}`), `message_start_run_c` and
  `message_delta_run_c` (all keys and values of lines 4 and 124). There are also the consts `RUN_C_THINKING`,
  `RUN_C_TEXT`, `RUN_C_ARGS` and `RUN_C_TOOL_USE_ID`.
- `ThinkingToolCallCleanStop`'s script did not change.
- The `anthropic` module doc: the sentence "this suite has no reasoning-delta scenario for any subject" is
  replaced. The `thinking_text_tool_use.txt` bullet now records that run C is `ReasoningCleanStop`'s
  script.
- `scan_finds_only_a_populated_stop_reason` now also checks that `message_delta_run_c` carries the marker
  and that the four new non-terminal frames do not.

## Tests and results

New tests in the `lib.rs` tests module:

- `a_reasoning_run_after_the_text_run_fails`: gives
  `ChannelOrderMismatch { expected: [Reasoning, Text, Tool], observed: [Text, Reasoning, Tool] }`.
- `a_reasoning_scenario_without_reasoning_fails`: `InsufficientEvidence` containing `"no ReasoningDelta"`.
- `a_reasoning_scenario_without_a_declared_order_fails`: `InsufficientEvidence` containing
  `"declares no channel order"`.
- Item (a), `a_declined_outcome_for_an_uncaptured_pair_fails`: a mock `bedrock` returns
  `Outcome::Declined("no captured reasoning stream")` for `ReasoningCleanStop`, which only `UNCAPTURED`
  pins. The test runs `assert_conforms` in a `tokio::spawn` and reads the panic message. It asserts that
  the message contains **both** `"unexpected decline of ReasoningCleanStop"` (the `DECLINED` check) and
  `"ReasoningCleanStop is pinned as uncaptured"` (the `UNCAPTURED` check). It passes.

### TDD evidence

RED: `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance` (after I wrote the tests, before the
implementation):

```text
   1 error: could not compile `paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance` (lib test) due to 39 previous errors
   6 error[E0061]: this function takes 4 arguments but 5 arguments were supplied
   1 error[E0407]: method `fixture_channel_order` is not a member of trait `StreamUnderTest`
   3 error[E0425]: cannot find type `Channel` in this scope
   1 error[E0432]: unresolved import `crate::Channel`
  12 error[E0433]: cannot find type `Channel` in this scope
   1 error[E0599]: no variant named `ChannelOrderMismatch` found for enum `Violation`
  15 error[E0599]: no variant, associated function, or constant named `ReasoningCleanStop` found for enum `Scenario` in the current scope
```

GREEN: `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance` (final tree):

```text
test result: ok. 72 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.82s
test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.88s
test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 0.00s
```

The six `conforms` tests pass. The stop rule did not apply.

Also clean: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`,
`cargo clippy -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and
`RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc -p paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance --no-deps`.

### The channel-order check runs on the real anthropic stream (Review Focus 5)

I changed the anthropic declaration to `[Text, Reasoning, Tool]` for one run, then reverted it. The run
failed as expected:

```text
conformance: anthropic / ReasoningCleanStop — ChannelOrderMismatch { expected: [Text, Reasoning, Tool], observed: [Reasoning, Text, Tool] }
  observed: Usage, ReasoningDelta x15, ProviderData{block: thinking, signature SIG_FAKE_1, index 0}, TokenDelta x12,
  ProviderData{index 1, kind text}, ToolCallDelta(toolu_017EB2o3zrXW8R73aqBPNiZi, name=get_weather), ToolCallDelta x3,
  ProviderData{call_id toolu_017..., index 2, kind tool_use}, Usage, Finish(ToolCalls)
```

(The `observed:` line is shortened here. The full line names each event.) The observed order is
`[Reasoning, Text, Tool]`, the same as the capture. The translator emits no empty `TokenDelta` for
the text block's `"text":""` start, and no `ReasoningDelta` for the thinking block's `"thinking":""` start.
The empty first `input_json_delta` gives a `ToolCallDelta` that is part of the tool run. The accumulated
thinking text in the `ProviderData` block is exactly the concatenation of the 15 captured fragments.

### Item (b): the five static tests in `src/declines.rs` fail on a bad row

For each test, I added one bad row, ran `cargo test ... --lib declines::`, and restored the file from a
backup (`cmp` confirmed it was unchanged). None of the bad rows is committed.

| Test | Bad row | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `no_pair_is_in_both_tables` | `DECLINED` row `("bedrock", ReasoningCleanStop, "x")` | FAILED (only this test) |
| `every_uncaptured_subject_is_registered` | `UNCAPTURED` row with subject `"bedrok"` | FAILED (only this test) |
| `every_follow_up_is_a_linear_id` | the `bedrock` row's follow-up changed to `"SMA858"` | FAILED (only this test) |
| `every_scenario_has_a_serving_subject` | `UNCAPTURED` row `("anthropic", ReasoningCleanStop, ...)` | FAILED (only this test) |
| `uncaptured_rows_name_only_allow_listed_scenarios` | `UNCAPTURED` row `("gemini", CleanStop, ...)` | FAILED (only this test) |

A first try at the follow-up check used an `anthropic` row with `"858"`. It failed two tests, because the
row also took away the only serving subject. I repeated it with the `bedrock` row change above, which
failed only `every_follow_up_is_a_linear_id`.

## Files changed

- /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/lib.rs
- /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/fakes.rs
- /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/src/declines.rs
- /Users/smaschek/dev/paigasus/paigasus-helikon/.worktrees/sma-567/tests/provider-stream-conformance/tests/conformance.rs

## Self-review findings

- Every `match` on `Scenario` that I added or extended in `tests/conformance.rs` is exhaustive with no `_`
  arm. The non-anthropic `fixture_channel_order` methods return `None` with no match, because they make no
  claim for any scenario. The mock `Subject` in `lib.rs` already had a `_` arm in
  `fixture_finish_reason`. I left it.
- Clippy reported `type_complexity` on the mock `Subject::conforming`. I fixed it with a local
  `type Pinned` alias in the tests module.
- The reasons in `tests/conformance.rs` are literal strings that I typed by hand. They are not looked up
  from the tables.
- The floor order puts the "no ReasoningDelta" check before the declared-order check and the order
  comparison, so a stream without reasoning gets the more exact diagnosis.

## Concerns

1. **The tool name (a decision the coordinator should confirm).** Run C calls `lookup_city_code`. But
   `fixture_tool_name()` gives one name for each subject (`get_weather` for anthropic). The spec keeps it
   unchanged (§6.3), and the brief gives `ReasoningCleanStop` the tool floors, which check that name. The
   brief also says "`request()` offers the tool that the capture calls". I cannot follow all three rules. I
   chose to rename the call to `get_weather` in the script, record that as edit 2 in the provenance comment,
   and let `request()` offer `get_weather`. The arguments (`{"city": "Paris"}`) and the `tool_use` id are
   unchanged. The other choices were these:
   - (a) keep `lookup_city_code` and skip the name floor for this scenario, which makes a floor weaker;
   - (b) make `fixture_tool_name` depend on the scenario, which changes a trait that the spec keeps fixed.
   If the reviewer prefers (a) or (b), the change is small.
2. The mock `Subject::conforming(name)` now panics for an unknown name. All current tests use
   `openai/chat`, `anthropic` or `bedrock`.
